record.title: DRYLAB-Bench reports elevated assay-based biosecurity risk scores in tool-augmented model evaluations
record.summary: A new preprint reports DRYLAB-Bench, an in-silico evaluation of biological-design outputs from 15 frontier language models across 30 policy-derived scenarios, scored against 187,695 pre-existing deep-mutational-scan measurements. The authors report that 67.6% of one-shot designs exceeded the average measured variant and 21.4% fell in the assay-specific highest-risk decile; under their tool-augmented iterative workflow, the top-decile share rose to 23.5% and the pooled Biosecurity Risk Score increased by 0.116 standard deviations. These are author-reported results from single-substitution assay proxies, not evidence of multi-variant organism-level outcomes, physical construction, or real-world harm. The paper’s sequential design does not isolate whether tool outputs or the additional deliberation cause the full increase, and no independent reproduction was inspected.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors introduce DRYLAB-Bench, an in-silico benchmark that scores model-proposed designs against 187,695 pre-existing deep-mutational-scan measurements across 30 policy-derived scenarios.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that 67.6% of one-shot designs exceeded the average measured variant and 21.4% fell in the assay-specific highest-risk decile across their 15-model evaluation.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report a 23.5% highest-risk-decile share and a +0.116 standard-deviation pooled risk-score increase in their tool-augmented iterative workflow.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_SCOPE_LIMITATION
claims.text: The paper limits its measurements to single-substitution assay proxies and does not claim multi-variant organism-level or physical-construction outcomes.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_SCOPE_LIMITATION
claims.text: The paper states that its study does not isolate the effect of tool-output content from the additional deliberation induced by tool rounds.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of the benchmark scoring, model runs or aggregate risk results was inspected.
The score is bounded to single-substitution assay measurements and does not establish multi-variant effects, host-context biology, transmission, or operational real-world risk.
The within-trajectory comparison does not isolate the causal contribution of tool-output content from extra deliberation; the paper describes two unrun mechanism controls.

brief.importance_rationale: If replicated, evidence that frontier models can prioritize measured high-risk single-substitution designs and that a tool-augmented workflow raises assay-based scores could shift biosecurity evaluation and tool-access decisions across frontier AI programs. A 7 reflects cross-team significance while the preprint, assay-bounded proxy, single-substitution scope and unresolved workflow mechanism keep the claim short of a field-reset result.
limitations: Results are reported by the paper authors in a single preprint and were not independently reproduced in this activation.

The Biosecurity Risk Score is an assay-relative proxy based on single-substitution measurements; it does not establish multi-variant phenotypes, organism-level behavior, transmission or real-world harm.
The study’s sequential conditions do not fully separate tool-output effects from extra deliberation; the authors identify further controls that are not run.
The paper includes sensitive adversarial prompts and biological examples; this public record retains only high-level methods and aggregate results.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report that 67.6% of one-shot designs exceeded the average measured variant and 21.4% fell in the assay-specific top decile. In tool-augmented iterative conditions, they report a 23.5% top-decile share and a pooled Biosecurity Risk Score increase of +0.116 standard deviations.
technical.demonstrated_result: The inspected arXiv v1 paper documents the benchmark design and reports results for 15 frontier models across 30 scenarios. Those reported measurements have not been independently reproduced in this activation.
technical.mechanism: The authors compare model-proposed single-substitution designs in one-shot and tool-augmented iterative settings, scoring them against pre-existing deep-mutational-scan measurements. The benchmark reports assay-relative risk proxies and does not perform biological synthesis.
technical.regime: Author-run in-silico evaluation of 15 frontier models across 30 policy-derived scenarios, with scores mapped to 187,695 pre-existing ProteinGym/ViroGym single-substitution assay measurements. It does not measure multi-variant effects, host context, transmission or physical construction.
technical.strongest_baseline: The strongest within-paper baseline is the same model’s pre-tool one-shot submission in the same sequential trajectory. The authors also report single-round and repeated no-tool controls, but the no-tool iteration arm is under-sampled and noisy.

brief.title: DRYLAB-Bench reports elevated assay-based biosecurity risk scores in tool-augmented model evaluations
brief.why_it_matters: If the reported assay-bounded results replicate, this evaluation moves biosecurity assessment beyond knowledge and refusal tests toward empirical measurement of model-generated designs and tool-augmented workflows. That could change how developers evaluate access to computational design tools. The measured single-substitution assay outcomes do not establish organism-level effects or operational threat.
